To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tolerances on the PETS misalignments, drive beam injection jitter and drive beam energy spread are 0.1 mm, 0.5 ns and 0.1%, respectively.
the tolerances on the drive beam position and injection jitter are of the order of a few tens of micrometres.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of the wakefield excited in the main linac couplers by PETS misalignments and drive beam injection errors.
the effects of the external wakefield from the CLiC PETS.
the impact of the external wakefield generated by the CLIC PESTS on the beam dynamics in the main linac.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PETS wake is not a show stopper for the CLIC drive beam concept.
the tolerances on the PETS alignment are in the order of 1-2 μm, depending on the PETS location in the linac.
the beam quality degradation due to the external wakefields is negligible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a misalignment of 0.1 mm in the PETS would result in a beam energy spread of 0.2% and a transverse emittance growth of 0.3% for the 12.5 GeV drive beam and the 5.0 TeV main beam.
a misalignment of 10 µm of the PETS with respect to the main linac structure will lead to 1.2% energy spread and 1.5% emittance growth for a single bunch.
a misalignment tolerance of 0.5 mm for the PETS and a drive beam jitter tolerance of 1.5 ps are required to meet CLIC’s beam quality requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tolerances on the PETS position and on the drive beam injection jitter can be relaxed if the drive beam energy spread is kept below 1.5%.
, in the single-bunch regime, the tolerance on the PETS misalignment and drive beam injection timing jitter is in the order of 1 μm.
the tolerances on the PETS position and drive beam jitter are very demanding.
